A1.justification: Both 45-page PDFs describe XR-1 and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The material can be reliably matched despite appendix relabeling and layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original robotic evaluations, ablations, generalization experiments and CALVIN simulation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including robotic success rates, representation analyses and CALVIN evaluations.

M1.justification: The dual-branch VQ-VAE, shared codebook, alignment loss and three-stage XR-1 training procedure are unchanged. The single-modality variants newly displayed in Table 3 already appear in v2 Table 14.

E1.justification: Both versions use Open-X, RoboMIND, XR-D and Ego4D, with the same robotic embodiments, manipulation tasks, CALVIN evaluation and generalization scenarios. The full task specifications in Table 19 are unchanged.

E2.justification: The robotic, fast-adaptation and CALVIN comparator sets are unchanged. The additional variant rows in v3 Table 3 reproduce comparisons already reported in v2 Tables 14–15.

E3.justification: Table 15 changes Stage-2 training for both Ego4D ablation variants from XR-D in v2 to DT, meaning downstream task data, in v3. This is a reported setting revision; the unchanged scores and accompanying prose do not establish whether experiments were rerun. Other evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: The ablation questions and reported outcomes are retained. Motion-only, vision-only and Ego4D results added to Table 3 already appear in v2 Tables 14–15. Robustness, transfer, retrieval and failure analyses are unchanged; the Ego4D training-setting revision is assessed under E3.

E5.justification: Trial-count disclosures and statistical reporting are unchanged, including 20 rollouts per robotic task and the similarity summaries in Table 18. No new seed information, uncertainty intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and qualitative findings are retained. The 35.0%, 50.0%, 32.5% and 38.3% averages newly displayed in Table 3 already occur in v2 Tables 14–15. The Ego4D scores remain unchanged despite the revised Stage-2 label.

T1.justification: The reconstruction and alignment objectives, policy-loss definitions and appendix nearest-neighbor similarity derivation are unchanged. No formal assumptions, propositions or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about UVMC, three-stage learning, cross-embodiment transfer and performance against the same baselines.

C2.justification: Interpretations involving multimodal alignment, reduced optimization conflicts and transferable representations are retained. The limitations concerning precision and bimanual coordination are also unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds Appendix A with direct links to the XR-1 code repository and model-weight collections on HuggingFace and ModelScope, supplementing the existing project-page link. Architecture, hyperparameter, hardware and training-time disclosures are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Reference updates match the same works across preprint and publication records, such as π0 and HybridVLA. They change bibliographic metadata rather than cited-work membership or the research positioning in Section 2.

P1.justification: A short resource appendix and funding acknowledgment are added, with appendix letters, cross-references and bibliographic metadata updated. The narrative is otherwise retained, including experiment-number references in Section 4.3 that become incorrect after Table 3 is expanded.

P2.justification: Table 3 expands from 10 to 14 rows by redisplaying appendix results and renumbering experiments. Figure 7 moves from page 9 to page 10, and Table 8 has a different page break. The overall visual design and remaining scientific displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves resource findability and brings existing ablations into the main table. However, Section 4.3 retains stale references: its 66.7% 'Exp. 5' now points to motion-only performance of 35.0%, while 66.7% has moved to Exp. 7. These internal-consistency costs, together with the unexplained Ego4D setting revision, leave the net quality effect unclear.
